text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz criticised right-wing opposition parties for urging Poles to reject the parliamentary constitution bill in a referendum on May 25.

- It is the EU's moral obligation to let central and eastern European countries share welfare and stable democracy which were made possible in the West thanks to the Marshall Plan, EU Commissioner Leon Brittan said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The centrist Union for Freedom (UW) leader Leszek Balcerowicz has criticised the ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) for halting economic reforms and the right-wing Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) for a political programme which combines mutually exclusive statements.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Polish-Finnish agreement on converting Poland's debt to Finland into funding for environmental protection schemes will be extended to 2000. Hitherto, the so-called eco-conversion of debts to Finland financed 31 schemes worth 65 million markka.
- The Polish-Lithuanian trade exchange reached $340 million in 1996 with Poland reporting a trade surplus of $110 million.

- The listed Stalexport foreign trade firm expects that the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will buy its D-series shares worth up to $30 million this year, Stalexport's president Ryszard Harhala said.
- The Niwka mining machinery plant has received the International Standards Organisation (ISO)- 9001 product quality certificate awarded by Germany's TUV Rheinland firm.
- The Pozmeat meat processing plant in Poznan is planning to sell one million shares priced at minimum 25 zlotys per share in a public offering in June, the firm said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- One of the five Boeing aircraft recently bought by the national air carrier LOT arrived at the Warsaw airport on Saturday. LOT now operates five Boeing planes.
- The structure of Poland's imports is not advantageous as it is dominated by consumer and inventory imports, the government's strategic studies centre president Zbigniew Kuzmiuk said.
- Around 60 percent of Poles would buy life insurance policies if they were allowed to deduct them from their taxable income, a survey by insurance firms said.
- Inter Fortuna Zycie (life) has received an operating licence from the State Insurance Supervision Office (PUNU). Inter Fortuna Zycie is Poland's nineteenth life insurer.
- The listed Swarzedz furniture maker's sales were 11.069 million in April showing a 21 percent growth compared with the same period in 1996, the firm's spokesman Sebastian Szczesny said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Unibud construction firm's shares will start continuous trade on the Warsaw bourse's main market on May 27, the company said. Unibud is a subsidiary of the Budimex construction firm.
ZYCIE
- An average Pole drinks 6.5 litres of juice a year, a survey by the Pentor polling institute said. In western Europe the average per capita juice consumption is 35 litres.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
